rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials (oval, s-bend, slalom; 20 each) ended off_track with 0 finishes. Progress reached only 0.10 to 0.14, and max_error hit about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit. Steering oscillation was low (0.07 to 0.14), so the failure is drift away from the line, not jitter. Each run logged about one line-loss event early on.

Diagnosis: with 2 cm sensor spacing and 12 mm footprints, the gaps between footprints are wider than the 25 mm tape can bridge. A 1 cm lateral offset is handled, but an offset of 2 to 3 cm can lose the line, and the robot then drifts out. Meanwhile kp=3 with signal up to +/-2 gives up to 2100 PWM of differential, and base_speed 1.6 gives little time to correct. The robot is over-driven for its sensing.

Changes: (1) Sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 with sensor_size 0.016, so footprints overlap and cover the tape continuously across the whole band. The outer sensors still see the line before it leaves the track. Sensor y stays at 0.04. (2) Weights stay proportional to x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the sign convention is unchanged. (3) base_speed 1.6 to 1.2 so the robot can correct on bends; the 3 s limit may be missed, so this is a trade-off. (4) kp 3.0 to 2.0 to reduce over-steering. (5) kd 0.15 to 0.3 to damp the faster response. (6) ki 0.05 to 0.02 to limit windup on the bends. (7) Mass, wheels and body unchanged, so the geometry change is limited to sensing.

Expected result: longer progress (target over 0.5) and fewer off-track ends, with line_loss_events near 0 and rms_error below 0.03 m. If the run now completes but slowly, raise base_speed in small steps. Hypotheses to test: (H1) sensor coverage is the main cause of line loss; (H2) kp 2.0 with kd 0.3 is stable at 1.2 m/s. Measurements requested: progress per track, line_loss_events, max_error, and steering_oscillation, so I can tell whether drift is from sensing or from speed.
